record.original_question: When phase retrieval is posed with a random sensing matrix A and the unknown object is uniformly distributed on the complex unit sphere, how do the statistical properties of A determine the smallest oversampling ratio alpha at which reconstruction becomes better than a random guess, and the smallest oversampling ratio at which the Bayes-optimal mean-squared error reaches the best value achievable for that sensing model?

evidence.quote: Question 6.2. Depending on statistical properties of the random measurement matrix A, what is the smallest value of α for which the reconstructed approximation of f0 is better than a random guess? What is the smallest value of α for which the average reconstruction error is as small as can be achieved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the complex phase retrieval problem in the high-dimensional proportional regime. Let n,m be positive integers with m/n → α > 0 as n → ∞ (α is called the oversampling ratio). Let f₀ be drawn uniformly at random from the complex unit sphere {f ∈ ℂⁿ : ‖f‖₂ = 1}. Let A ∈ ℂ^{m×n} be a random sensing matrix drawn from some prescribed ensemble (for instance, an i.i.d. Gaussian ensemble, a uniformly sampled partial unitary/Fourier ensemble, or, more generally, a right-unitarily-invariant ensemble characterized by a limiting singular value distribution). One observes the intensity measurements y = |A f₀|² ∈ ℝ^m (componentwise modulus squared, possibly with additional noise specified by a fixed channel). Let f̂(y, A) denote the Bayes-optimal estimator of f₀ (with respect to the global phase ambiguity, e.g. the estimator minimizing the expected projector distance to f₀), and let

   MMSE(α) = lim_{n→∞} 𝔼[ 1 − |⟨f̂, f₀⟩|² ].

Define:
 (a) the weak-recovery threshold α_WR as the infimum of α > 0 such that MMSE(α) is strictly smaller than the value attained by a uniformly random guess on the unit sphere;
 (b) the full-recovery threshold α_FR as the infimum of α > 0 such that MMSE(α) equals the smallest value achievable by any estimator for the given sensing model (i.e., the optimum over all measurable estimators in the chosen ensemble).

Determine, as explicit functionals of the statistical properties of the sensing ensemble (in particular its limiting singular value distribution), the values of α_WR and α_FR.
artifact.status_search_result: For i.i.d. Gaussian sensing matrices the weak-recovery threshold is known to be α_WR = 1 and full/strong recovery occurs at α_FR = 2 (Mondelli–Montanari and follow-ups). For right-unitarily-invariant ensembles with general spectrum, recent works derive single-letter formulas for the Bayes-optimal MMSE and for the (algorithmic) weak-recovery threshold, giving partial answers depending on the spectrum (e.g. unitary/Fourier ensembles yield thresholds at 2, while structured ensembles can shift them). A complete characterization of both thresholds for arbitrary sensing-matrix statistics remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fundamental Limits of Weak Recovery with Applications to Phase Retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: For i.i.d. random sensing matrices the weak-recovery threshold is α_WR = 1 and full recovery threshold α_FR = 2.
status_evidence.claim: Thresholds are established for the Gaussian i.i.d. case.

status_evidence.title: Towards Designing Optimal Sensing Matrices for Generalized Linear Inverse Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Single-letter formula for Bayes-optimal estimator with right-unitarily-invariant sensing matrices and arbitrary spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Bayes-optimal MMSE is characterized for unitarily invariant ensembles, giving partial answers for α_FR.

status_evidence.title: Construction of optimal spectral methods in phase retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic weak-recovery threshold derived as function of singular value distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Weak-recovery threshold is characterized in terms of spectrum for broader ensembles.
